facts.text: SAMPLE: Roman concrete set underwater. Some harbours built two thousand years ago are still standing.
SAMPLE: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
SAMPLE: Viking ships sat low in the water, so raiders could row far up shallow rivers.
SAMPLE: In the Christmas Truce of 1914, soldiers on both sides left their trenches and met in no man's land.
SAMPLE: Leonardo da Vinci wrote his notebooks in mirror writing, from right to left.
SAMPLE: At its peak the Mongol Empire covered roughly a sixth of the world's land.
SAMPLE: Sputnik 1 launched in 1957 and orbited Earth for about three months before falling back.
SAMPLE: During the French Revolution, France adopted a ten-day week and ten-hour days. Neither lasted long.
SAMPLE: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, after a gap of about 1,500 years.
SAMPLE: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in 1825, the first public railway to use steam locomotives.
SAMPLE: In 1962 a Soviet officer, Vasili Arkhipov, refused to agree to a nuclear torpedo launch.
SAMPLE: The Dow Jones took until 1954 to climb back to its September 1929 peak.
